Proton Pump Inhibitors

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Mechanism of Action

PPIs are prodrugs with enteric coating

They get absorbed in the intestine to blood

PPIs work on the parietal cells in the stomach

PPIs irreversibly inhibit gastric hydrogen potassium ATPase (H+/K+) ATPase Which is the final step of acid secretion in the stomach

that is why PPIs are the most effective at inhibiting gastric acid

PPIs have short half lives (around 1.5 hours) but acid inhibition lasts up to 24 hours because of irreversible inactivation of the proton pumps

6 PPI agents

Omeprazole

Esomeprazole

Lansoprazole

Dexlansoprazole

Rabeprazole

Pantoprazole

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

PPIs clinical uses

GERD, erosive esophagitis

Peptic ulcer disease

H pylori infection

NSAID-associated ulcers

GIT bleeding due to ulcer

Non ulcer dyspepsia

Gastrinoma and hypersecretory conditions

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Adverse Effects

Nausea, Diarrhea, Headache, GI disturbance

Decrease effectiveness of some drugs like clopidogrel when used with omeprazole and esomeprazole. Because they inhibit CYP2C19 which is involved in converting clopidogrel to its active metabolites

Increase risk of fractures

Decrease vitamin B12 absorption

Increase gastric cancer risk
